name: audio_pitch_harmonics
expr: f220 = pitch(x220, fs); f100 = pitch(x100, fs); h220 = harmonicRatio(x220, fs); pn220 = numel(f220); hn220 = numel(h220); f220_first = f220(1); f220_mean = mean(f220); f100_mean = mean(f100); h220_mean = mean(h220); fcep220 = pitch(x220, fs, 'Method', 'CEP'); cep_first = fcep220(1); cep_2 = fcep220(2); cep_4 = fcep220(4); cep_mean = mean(fcep220); fpef220 = pitch(x220, fs, 'Method', 'PEF'); pef_first = fpef220(1); pef_mean = mean(fpef220); xmix = sin(2*pi*220*t) + 0.5*sin(2*pi*100*t); fpef_range = pitch(xmix, fs, 'Method', 'PEF', 'Range', [80 250]); pef_r_first = fpef_range(1); flhs220 = pitch(x220, fs, 'Method', 'LHS'); lhs_first = flhs220(1); lhs_2 = flhs220(2); lhs_mean = mean(flhs220); fsrh220 = pitch(x220, fs, 'Method', 'SRH'); srh_n = numel(fsrh220);
comment: pitch + harmonicRatio (Audio Toolbox). Methods: NCF (default), CEP, PEF, LHS, SRH. CEP/LHS/SRH have been clean-room reimplemented from public papers as part of the IP-provenance remediation (see cleanroom/). CEP (Noll 1967) and LHS (Hermes 1988) are bit-identical to MATLAB R2025b. SRH is a faithful implementation of the published method (Drugman & Alwan, Interspeech 2011); MATLAB's SRH pipeline diverges from the paper in undocumented ways, so numkit's SRH is intentionally NOT bit-matched to MATLAB — srh_first is excluded from the cross-engine fingerprint (srh_n, the frame count, still matches). NCF and PEF parity unchanged (PEF clean-room rewrite still pending). harmonicRatio: auto low-edge + Smith parabolic. Tolerance 5%; pitchnn deferred (DNN runtime not in numkit).
